data_description.scan_method: 'Auto' uses nmap when available and falls back to a ping and ARP sweep.

data_description.port_scan: A second pass that connects to the listed ports on online devices. Off by default.

data_description.port_scan_interval: Open ports rarely change: 1800 s (30 min) is a good value. Minimum 60 s.
data_description.default_open_port: 0 = choose automatically from the open ports (443/8443 → https, 80/8123/8080 → http). Otherwise always use this port.

data_description.watch_message: Sent both when a watched device becomes unreachable and when it comes back.
data_description.recovery_title: Jinja template used when a monitored device becomes reachable again.
data_description.recovery_message: Separate from the outage message: the two events say different things.

about.title: Про компонент
about.description:
## {name}
**Версія {version}** — By **{author}**

Watches the local network, recognises devices Home Assistant already knows, and alerts you when an unauthorised one shows up.

---

### What it does

**Network scanning**  
Sweeps the subnet on a schedule with nmap, falling back to a ping and ARP sweep when nmap is unavailable. A device is only marked offline after several missed scans in a row, so one lost packet never raises a false alarm.

**Unauthorised device alerts**  
Any device that is not on the trusted list and answers a scan is flagged, raises an event and triggers a notification the first time it appears.

**Availability monitoring**  
A separate list of critical devices whose reachability matters. When one stops answering you get an alert with how long it has been down, and a second alert when it comes back. Router, DNS server, Zigbee coordinators, NVR.

**Device identification**  
Names come from the Home Assistant device registry, from the device's own web interface (vendor JSON endpoints and page titles) and from the hardware vendor behind the MAC address, in that order.

**Open port detection**  
Optional second pass that probes the configured ports over TCP and labels the well-known ones. Web ports produce a direct link to the device's interface.

**Sidebar panel**  
A full page listing every device with search, filters, inline renaming, free-text notes and one-click trust or monitoring.

**Notifications**  
Push, email or any notify target, with Jinja templates you can rewrite for each of the three events.

---

### Current status

| | |
|---|---|
| Watched network | `{subnet}` |
| Scan method | `{method}` · {interval} s |
| Last scan | {last_scan} |
| Known devices | **{total}** |
| Online now | **{online}** |
| Unauthorised | **{anomalous}** |
| Whitelisted | **{whitelist}** |
| Monitored devices | **{watched}** |
| Monitored offline | **{watched_offline}** |
| Port detection | `{ports}` |
| Sidebar panel | `{panel}` |
| Named via web | **{named}** |

---

### Entities

- `sensor.network_anomalous_devices`
- `sensor.network_online_devices`
- `sensor.network_watched_offline`
- `binary_sensor.network_new_device_detected`

### Services

`scan_now` · `add_to_whitelist` · `remove_from_whitelist` · `forget_device` · `add_to_watchlist` · `remove_from_watchlist`

### Events

`network_device_monitor_new_device` · `network_device_monitor_anomalous_device` · `network_device_monitor_watched_device_down` · `network_device_monitor_watched_device_up`

abort.whitelist_empty: There are no UI-managed trusted devices to remove.
abort.not_loaded: The integration is not loaded; fix the setup error first.

scan_now.name: Scan now
scan_now.description: Run a network scan immediately instead of waiting for the next cycle.

add_to_whitelist.name: Add to whitelist
add_to_whitelist.description: Mark a device as trusted so it stops raising notifications.

mac.name: MAC address
mac.description: MAC address of the device to trust.

ip.name: IP address
ip.description: IP address, used when the MAC address is unknown.

name.name: Name
name.description: Friendly name stored alongside the whitelist entry.

remove_from_whitelist.name: Remove from whitelist
remove_from_whitelist.description: Stop trusting a device. Only UI-managed entries can be removed.

device.name: Device
device.description: MAC or IP address of the whitelist entry to remove.

forget_device.name: Forget device
forget_device.description: Drop a device from the inventory so it is treated as new next time it appears.

device.name: Device
device.description: MAC or IP address of the device to forget.
